messages.body_plain:
Hi Natalia,

On your questions:

My understanding is that scale_datetime() is a special case of a numerical scale; you have set a nominal scale for "x" by virtue of using ~factor(x). I think this is the source of the problem.

Would it work to keep the x-scale numeric and to specify the extent of the rectangle using the data:

master$x2 <- master$x + 60 # adds 60 seconds to x

then define the rectangles accordingly:

layer_rects(x2 = ~x2, height = band(), fill.brush := "red", opacity := 0.3)

For the fill colors to match the factor, something like this could work:

scale_nominal("fill", domain = c("red", "yellow", "blue"), range = c("red", "yellow", "blue"))

all together:

    master %>%
      ggvis(~x,~y,fill=~factor ) %>%
      layer_rects(x2 = ~x2, height = band(), fill.brush := "red", opacity := 0.3) %>%
      lb$input() %>%
      scale_nominal("fill", domain = c("red", "yellow", "blue"), range = c("red", "yellow", "blue")) %>%

      scale_nominal("y", padding = 0, points = FALSE) %>%
      bind_shiny("plot1")

Hope this helps,

Ian

messages.body_plain:
Here's a working example:

cocaine %>%
  ggvis(~potency, ~price) %>%

  filter(state %in% eval(input_checkboxgroup(c("IA", "MN", "WI"),
selected = "WI"))) %>%

  layer_points(fill = ~state, size := 50, opacity := 0.5)

I made two changes:

* Both dplyr and ggvis using non-standard evaluation in slightly
different ways, so filter() needs a bit of a hint that
input_checkboxgroup() should be evaluated different. Surround it in
eval() to force it to be evaluated eagerly (this is documented in
filter.ggvis)

* Currently the default selected value is NULL, which selects no
values, and hence ggvis tries to plot an empty data frame and fails
(this is a bug). So you also need to check at least one group by
default. I've filed an issue about this :
https://github.com/rstudio/ggvis/issues/272

Hadley

messages.body_plain:
I'm fairly new to the ggvis package and I'm trying to replicate some common plots I've made with ggplot2.  Right now I'm trying to replicate a line plot in which there are multiple lines for each level of a group.  For example, I'm trying to replicate a multiple line graph plotting the average length over the different dose groups for each level of supp using the ToothGrowth data set (example adapted from the Cookbook for R <http://www.cookbook-r.com/Graphs/Plotting_means_and_error_bars_%28ggplot2%29/> site and the R Graphics Cookbook <http://www.anrdoezrs.net/click-7028012-11260198?url=http%3A%2F%2Fshop.oreilly.com%2Fproduct%2F0636920023135.do&cjsku=0636920023135>):

# load data set
data(ToothGrowth)

# load dplyr
library(dplyr)

# summarize data set to get averange length for each supp and dose combination
tg <- ToothGrowth %>%
  group_by(supp, dose) %>%
  summarize(length = mean(len, na.rm = TRUE))

# create ggplot2 version of plot
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(tg, aes(x=dose, y=length, colour=supp)) + geom_line()

# create ggvis version of plot
library(ggvis)
tg %>%
  ggvis(~dose, ~length, stroke = ~supp) %>%
  layer_lines()

The ggplot2 version correctly shows only two lines with different colors, while the ggvis version is showing three lines and with the same color for each line.  How can I properly recreate this graph with ggvis?  Please see the attached images for each version of the plot.

Thanks,
Eric.

messages.subject_clean: I can't get ggvis scales to remain fixed with reactive input
messages.body_plain:
I've also posted this as a stackoverflow question.

I'm trying to create a shiny app that allows the user to select certain groups to plot on a ggvis graph. The problem I'm having is that if I map reactive data to properties of the points (like the point fill, shape, etc.), the scale resets every time the user updates the groups. So the mapping of group identity to fill color does not remain constant. I tried to fix this by hard coding group id to fill color in a reactive element, but then I start getting difficult to interpret errors when the app starts to load.

Here's my code for my first attempt at a solution:

#ui.R
library(shiny)
library(ggvis)

shinyUI(fluidPage(

  # Application title
  titlePanel("Old Faithful Geyser Data"),

  # Sidebar with a slider input for number of bins
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      checkboxGroupInput("gear", label = "Gears", choices = c("3","4","5"))
    ),

    # Show a plot of the generated distribution
    mainPanel(
      uiOutput("ggvis_ui"),
      ggvisOutput("ggvis"),
      textOutput("jawn"))
  )
))

#server.R
library(shiny)
library(ggvis)
library(dplyr)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

    selected <- reactive(input$gear)

    selectedData <- reactive({
      mtcars %>%
        filter(gear %in% selected())%>%
        mutate(gear = as.character(gear))
    })

    colorRange <- reactive({
      c(`3` = "red", `4` = "blue", `5` = "green")[sort(selected())]
    })

    output$jawn <- renderText(colorRange())

    mtcars%>%
      ggvis(~wt, ~mpg)%>%
      layer_points()%>%
      layer_points(data = selectedData, fill = ~gear)%>%
      scale_ordinal("fill", range = colorRange) %>%
      bind_shiny("ggvis", "ggvis_ui")
})

When I try to run the app, I get this error:

Error : x is not a numeric or integer vector

I've also created a github repository with one of my other attempts at a solution.

https://github.com/JoFrhwld/ggvis_scales

-Joe

Even better. If you group_by the categorizing data, the animation doesn't happen, I guess for some reason having to do with looking at row indexing or something? The comprehensive answer appears to be:

library(shiny)
library(ggvis)
library(dplyr)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

    selected <- reactive(input$gear)

    selectedData <- reactive({
      mtcars %>%
        filter(gear %in% selected())%>%

        mutate(gear = as.character(gear))%>%
        group_by(gear)
    })

    .domain <- c(3, 4, 5)
    .range <- c("red", "blue", "green")

    mtcars%>%
      ggvis(~wt, ~mpg)%>%
      layer_points()%>%
      layer_points(data = selectedData, fill = ~gear)%>%

      scale_ordinal("fill", range = .range, domain = .domain) %>%

      bind_shiny("ggvis", "ggvis_ui")
})

Added benefits: even when there's no data selected, the legend is populated.

Thanks!

-Joe
